economy.summary: His campaign platform says he will fight for smart economic growth to combat inflation and help create jobs in the region.
economy.short: Supports economic growth to combat inflation and create jobs.

taxes.summary: Supported the 2026-27 state budget agreement, saying it spends less than $51 billion, about $2.5 billion less than the governor's proposal, and avoids draining the Rainy Day Fund; his campaign platform calls for smart budgeting, low taxes, and less regulation.
taxes.short: Supported 2026 budget deal; calls for low taxes, smart budgeting.

abortion.summary: Voted against House Bill 1957, a proposed amendment to the Pennsylvania Constitution providing for personal reproductive liberty, which passed the state House 102-101 in December 2025.
abortion.short: Voted against proposed constitutional amendment on personal reproductive liberty.

education.summary: His campaign platform says he will improve education with accountability, parental involvement, and choice.
education.short: Supports education accountability, parental involvement, and choice.

energy.summary: Supported ending Pennsylvania's participation in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, saying the program cost the state energy jobs and economic development and that removing carbon taxes would jumpstart energy production; also co-introduced a bill to exempt Beaver County from vehicle emissions inspections.
energy.short: Supported RGGI exit; co-introduced Beaver County emissions inspection exemption.

guns.summary: His campaign platform says he will defend the Second Amendment, support law enforcement, and get tough on crime, especially violent criminals.
guns.short: Says he will defend Second Amendment and support law enforcement.
